title: [v0.4.x] MCP: classify expected preconditions correctly
author: mcpdev80
body:
## Current triage — outstanding pre-freeze work

Milestone: **v0.4.x**; final semantic acceptance: #174. Original v0.4.20/v0.4.21/v0.4.24 references below describe the historical report, not proof of completion or a new release assignment.

Some expected-precondition classification is now implemented in [main.go at `1b1ae323`](https://github.com/mcpdev80/baseharbor/blob/1b1ae323284d436f379777a3ab65b37072df14c3/cmd/baha/main.go), including workspace/manifest absence and organization configuration errors. That source inspection alone does not prove every MCP case in this issue. Keep open for bounded CLI/MCP verification of the listed organization, unknown application/deployment and workspace outcomes, cancellation and unexpected-error behavior; record the actual remaining failures rather than assuming the entire original defect is still present.

---

## Bug

Expected machine/MCP preconditions are currently flattened to `internal_error` because `machine.Classify` only preserves already-typed `*machine.Error` values.

Confirmed on v0.4.20 and still present on the active v0.4.21 release branch.

Affected examples include:

- organization configuration not configured
- unsupported organization source kind
- application has no registered deployment
- repository manifest not found for workspace operations

CLI output remains actionable, but MCP/agent automation cannot distinguish expected user/configuration state from an actual internal failure.

## Required behavior

Use stable typed machine codes for expected preconditions.

- missing registered application/deployment -> `not_found`
- repository manifest/workspace source absent -> `source_missing`
- organization configuration absent -> `validation_failed`
- unsupported organization source kind -> `unsupported_operation`
- actual internal/unclassified failures remain `internal_error`

## Acceptance

- [ ] `baseharbor.organization.inspect` without org config is not `internal_error`.
- [ ] unsupported organization source kind is not `internal_error`.
- [ ] `baseharbor.status` / `policy.explain` for unknown app return `not_found`.
- [ ] `baseharbor.workspace.status` outside an app repo returns `source_missing`.
- [ ] CLI and MCP use the same underlying typed error semantics.
- [ ] context timeout/cancellation behavior remains unchanged.
- [ ] unknown unexpected errors still classify as `internal_error`.
- [ ] focused machine/MCP tests and go vet pass.
- [ ] fix lands directly in active v0.4.21.

Related inspect fixes: #750 #751 #752
